```{r}
# PART 1: GENERATE SAMPLE DATASETS

set.seed(42)

# Create Texas Government Employee Data (TRS - Teacher Retirement System)
create_trs_data <- function(n = 500) {
  
  first_names <- c("John", "Maria", "Robert", "Jennifer", "Michael", "Sarah",
                   "David", "Patricia", "James", "Linda", "Daniel", "Barbara")
  last_names <- c("Smith", "Johnson", "Williams", "Brown", "Jones", "Garcia",
                  "Miller", "Davis", "Rodriguez", "Martinez", "Hernandez", "Lopez")
  
  trs <- tibble(
    record_id = paste0("TRS_", 1:n),
    first_name = sample(first_names, n, replace = TRUE),
    last_name = sample(last_names, n, replace = TRUE),
    dob = sample(seq(as.Date("1950-01-01"), as.Date("1985-12-31"), by = "day"), n),
    years_service = sample(5:40, n, replace = TRUE),
    salary_group = sample(c("Elementary", "Secondary", "Administration"), n, replace = TRUE),
    retirement_date = NA_Date_
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      # Some retirements for older employees
      retirement_date = case_when(
        years_service > 30 ~ as.Date(paste0(2020 + sample(0:4, n, replace = TRUE), 
                                              "-", 
                                              sample(1:12, n, replace = TRUE, prob = rep(1/12, 12)),
                                              "-01")),
        TRUE ~ NA_Date_
      )
    )
  
  return(trs)
}

# Create Education Agency Data (TEA - Texas Education Agency)
create_tea_data <- function(trs, n = 500, num_matches = 100, corruption_rate = 0.2) {
  
  first_names <- c("John", "Maria", "Robert", "Jennifer", "Michael", "Sarah",
                   "David", "Patricia", "James", "Linda", "Daniel", "Barbara",
                   "Jon", "Mary", "Rob", "Jen", "Mike", "Sara")  # Include variations
  last_names <- c("Smith", "Smithe", "Smyth", "Johnson", "Jonson", "Williams", 
                  "Brown", "Jones", "Garcia", "Miller", "Davis", "Rodriguez", 
                  "Martinez", "Hernandez", "Lopez", "Sanchez")
  
  tea <- tibble(
    record_id = paste0("TEA_", 1:n),
    first_name = sample(first_names, n, replace = TRUE),
    last_name = sample(last_names, n, replace = TRUE),
    dob = sample(seq(as.Date("1950-01-01"), as.Date("1985-12-31"), by = "day"), n),
    certification = sample(c("Science", "Math", "English", "Social Studies", "Special Ed"), n, replace = TRUE),
    school_district = sample(paste0("District_", 1:50), n, replace = TRUE),
    hire_date = sample(seq(as.Date("1990-01-01"), as.Date("2020-12-31"), by = "day"), n)
  )
  
  # Make the first num_matches TEA records true matches of TRS_1..TRS_num_matches.
  # The remaining TEA records are unrelated people (true non-matches).
  tea$first_name[1:num_matches] <- trs$first_name[1:num_matches]
  tea$last_name[1:num_matches] <- trs$last_name[1:num_matches]
  tea$dob[1:num_matches] <- trs$dob[1:num_matches]

  # Introduce data quality issues in the matched records only
  # About 20% of matched records have corruption or variation
  corruption_indices <- sample(1:num_matches, size = round(num_matches * corruption_rate), replace = FALSE)
  
  for (idx in corruption_indices) {
    flip <- sample(1:3, 1)
    
    if (flip == 1) {
      # Introduce name variation
      tea$first_name[idx] <- abbreviate(tea$first_name[idx], minlength = 3)
    } else if (flip == 2) {
      # Introduce small typo in last name
      last_chars <- nchar(tea$last_name[idx])
      if (last_chars > 1) {
        typo_pos <- sample(1:last_chars, 1)
        wrong_char <- sample(letters[!(letters %in% unlist(strsplit(tea$last_name[idx], "")))], 1)
        tea$last_name[idx] <- paste0(
          substr(tea$last_name[idx], 1, typo_pos - 1),
          wrong_char,
          substr(tea$last_name[idx], typo_pos + 1, last_chars)
        )
      }
    } else {
      # Shift DOB slightly (data entry error)
      tea$dob[idx] <- tea$dob[idx] + sample(c(-1, 1), 1)
    }
  }
  
  return(tea)
}

# Create a subset of KNOWN matches for validation
create_validation_set <- function(trs, tea, num_matches = 100) {
  
  # Take first 100 records from TRS
  trs_subset <- trs %>% slice(1:num_matches)
  
  # These are the "true" matches in TEA
  true_matches <- tea %>%
    slice(1:num_matches) %>%
    rename_with(~paste0("tea_", .), everything()) %>%
    rename(tea_record_id = tea_record_id)
  
  # Create ground truth
  validation <- tibble(
    trs_record_id = trs_subset$record_id,
    tea_record_id = true_matches$tea_record_id,
    is_match = TRUE
  )
  
  return(validation)
}


set.seed(42)
cat("Generating sample datasets...\n")
trs_data <- create_trs_data(500)
tea_data <- create_tea_data(trs_data, 500, corruption_rate = 0.20)
validation_set <- create_validation_set(trs_data, tea_data)

# Display sample
cat("\nSample TRS data:\n")
print(head(trs_data, 3))

cat("\nSample TEA data:\n")
print(head(tea_data, 3))

cat("\nGround truth validation set:\n")
print(head(validation_set, 5))
```

```{r}
standardize_names <- function(name) {
  name %>%
    tolower() %>%              # Convert to lowercase
    str_trim() %>%             # Remove leading/trailing whitespace
    str_squish() %>%           # Remove extra internal whitespace
    str_replace_all("[^a-z ]", "")  # Remove punctuation/special characters
}

standardize_date <- function(date_col) {
  as.Date(date_col)
}

standardize_zipcodes <- function(zip) {
  # Ensure 5-digit format
  zip <- as.character(zip)
  str_pad(zip, width = 5, side = "left", pad = "0")
}

# Create clean versions
trs_clean <- trs_data %>%
  mutate(
    first_name_std = standardize_names(first_name),
    last_name_std = standardize_names(last_name),
    first_initial = substr(first_name_std, 1, 1),
    dob_std = standardize_date(dob)
  )

tea_clean <- tea_data %>%
  mutate(
    first_name_std = standardize_names(first_name),
    last_name_std = standardize_names(last_name),
    first_initial = substr(first_name_std, 1, 1),
    dob_std = standardize_date(dob)
  )

cat("\nStandardized TRS sample (IDs and initials only):\n")
print(trs_clean %>% select(record_id, first_initial, years_service, salary_group) %>% head(3))
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# PART 3: DETERMINISTIC LINKAGE RULES
# ============================================================================

deterministic_linkage <- function(data_a, data_b, 
                                  id_col_a = "record_id", 
                                  id_col_b = "record_id") {
  
  log_info("Starting deterministic linkage...")
  
  matches <- tibble()
  remaining_a <- data_a
  remaining_b <- data_b
  
  # RULE 1: Exact match on last name + first name + DOB
  # (Highest confidence)
  log_info("Applying Rule 1: Last name + First name + DOB")
  
  rule1 <- remaining_a %>%
    inner_join(
      remaining_b,
      by = c("last_name_std" = "last_name_std",
             "first_name_std" = "first_name_std",
             "dob_std" = "dob_std"),
      suffix = c("_a", "_b")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      rule_applied = "Rule_1_FullName_DOB",
      confidence = 0.99
    ) %>%
    select(!!sym(paste0(id_col_a, "_a")), 
           !!sym(paste0(id_col_b, "_b")), 
           rule_applied, confidence)
  
  matches <- bind_rows(matches, rule1)
  
  # Remove matched records
  remaining_a <- anti_join(remaining_a, rule1, by = setNames("record_id_a", id_col_a))
  remaining_b <- anti_join(remaining_b, rule1, by = setNames("record_id_b", id_col_b))
  
  log_info(paste("Rule 1 found", nrow(rule1), "matches"))
  
  # RULE 2: Last name + First initial + DOB
  # (For records where first name varies slightly)
  log_info("Applying Rule 2: Last name + First initial + DOB")
  
  rule2 <- remaining_a %>%
    inner_join(
      remaining_b,
      by = c("last_name_std" = "last_name_std",
             "first_initial" = "first_initial",
             "dob_std" = "dob_std"),
      suffix = c("_a", "_b")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      rule_applied = "Rule_2_LastName_Initial_DOB",
      confidence = 0.95
    ) %>%
    select(record_id_a, record_id_b, rule_applied, confidence)

  matches <- bind_rows(matches, rule2)
  remaining_a <- anti_join(remaining_a, rule2, by = setNames("record_id_a", id_col_a))
  remaining_b <- anti_join(remaining_b, rule2, by = setNames("record_id_b", id_col_b))
  
  log_info(paste("Rule 2 found", nrow(rule2), "matches"))
  
  # RULE 3: Last name + First name + DOB within 1 day
  # (For data entry errors on DOB)
  log_info("Applying Rule 3: Last name + First name + DOB (±1 day)")
  
  rule3 <- remaining_a %>%
    cross_join(remaining_b, suffix = c("_a", "_b")) %>%
    filter(
      last_name_std_a == last_name_std_b,
      first_name_std_a == first_name_std_b,
      abs(as.numeric(difftime(dob_std_a, dob_std_b, units = "days"))) <= 1
    ) %>%
    select(record_id_a, record_id_b) %>%
    mutate(
      rule_applied = "Rule_3_DOBFlex",
      confidence = 0.90
    )

  if (nrow(rule3) > 0) {
    # Remove duplicates (keep first match only)
    rule3 <- rule3 %>% distinct(record_id_a, .keep_all = TRUE)
    matches <- bind_rows(matches, rule3)
    remaining_a <- anti_join(remaining_a, rule3, by = setNames("record_id_a", id_col_a))
    remaining_b <- anti_join(remaining_b, rule3, by = setNames("record_id_b", id_col_b))
  }
  
  log_info(paste("Rule 3 found", nrow(rule3), "matches"))
  
  result <- list(
    matches = matches,
    remaining_a = remaining_a,
    remaining_b = remaining_b,
    summary = tibble(
      Rule = c("Rule 1", "Rule 2", "Rule 3"),
      Matches = c(nrow(rule1), nrow(rule2), nrow(rule3))
    )
  )
  
  return(result)
}

# Execute deterministic linkage
det_result <- deterministic_linkage(trs_clean, tea_clean)

cat("\nDeterministic Linkage Summary:\n")
print(det_result$summary)

cat("\nFirst 5 deterministic matches:\n")
print(head(det_result$matches, 5))
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# PART 4: PROBABILISTIC LINKAGE - SIMILARITY SCORING
# ============================================================================

# Calculate string similarity using Jaro-Winkler
calculate_string_similarity <- function(str1, str2, method = "jw") {
  
  if (is.na(str1) | is.na(str2)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  
  # Jaro-Winkler returns distance (0-1), we want similarity
  1 - stringdist(str1, str2, method = method)
}

# More efficient: Use vectorized stringdistmatrix
calculate_similarity_efficient <- function(data_a_field, data_b_field) {
  
  dist_matrix <- stringdistmatrix(
    data_a_field,
    data_b_field,
    method = "jw",
    useNames = "strings"
  )
  
  # Convert distance to similarity (1 - distance)
  similarity <- 1 - dist_matrix
  
  return(similarity)
}

# For unmatched records, compute similarities
unmatched_a <- det_result$remaining_a
unmatched_b <- det_result$remaining_b

cat(paste("\nComputing probabilistic matches for", 
          nrow(unmatched_a), "unmatched records in TRS and",
          nrow(unmatched_b), "in TEA...\n"))

# Calculate similarities for each field
last_name_sim <- calculate_similarity_efficient(
  unmatched_a$last_name_std,
  unmatched_b$last_name_std
)

first_name_sim <- calculate_similarity_efficient(
  unmatched_a$first_name_std,
  unmatched_b$first_name_std
)

# DOB exact match (1 if exact, 0 if different, 0.95 if within 1 day)
dob_sim <- outer(
  as.numeric(unmatched_a$dob_std),
  as.numeric(unmatched_b$dob_std),
  function(x, y) {
    diff_days <- abs(x - y)
    ifelse(diff_days == 0, 1.0, ifelse(diff_days == 1, 0.95, 0.0))
  }
)

# Convert to dataframes for easier manipulation
all_comparisons <- expand_grid(
  idx_a = 1:nrow(unmatched_a),
  idx_b = 1:nrow(unmatched_b)
) %>%
  mutate(
    record_id_a = unmatched_a$record_id[idx_a],
    record_id_b = unmatched_b$record_id[idx_b],
    last_name_sim = last_name_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
    first_name_sim = first_name_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
    dob_sim = dob_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)]
  ) %>%
  select(record_id_a, record_id_b, last_name_sim, first_name_sim, dob_sim)

# Calculate weighted match score
all_comparisons <- all_comparisons %>%
  mutate(
    match_score = (
      last_name_sim * 0.40 +   # Last name most important
      first_name_sim * 0.30 +  # First name medium importance
      dob_sim * 0.30           # DOB medium importance
    )
  )

cat("\nMatch score distribution:\n")
print(all_comparisons %>%
  summarise(
    min = min(match_score),
    q25 = quantile(match_score, 0.25),
    median = median(match_score),
    q75 = quantile(match_score, 0.75),
    max = max(match_score),
    n = n()
  ))

# Apply thresholds
probabilistic_matches <- all_comparisons %>%
  mutate(
    classification = case_when(
      match_score > 0.95 ~ "LINK",
      match_score >= 0.85 & match_score <= 0.95 ~ "REVIEW",
      TRUE ~ "NO_LINK"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(classification %in% c("LINK", "REVIEW"))

cat("\nProbabilistic matches by classification:\n")
print(probabilistic_matches %>%
  count(classification))

cat("\nSample LINK decisions (high confidence):\n")
print(probabilistic_matches %>%
  filter(classification == "LINK") %>%
  head(5))

cat("\nSample REVIEW decisions (uncertain):\n")
print(probabilistic_matches %>%
  filter(classification == "REVIEW") %>%
  head(5))
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# PART 5: VALIDATION AND QUALITY ASSESSMENT

# Combine deterministic and probabilistic matches
all_matches <- bind_rows(
  det_result$matches %>%
    select(record_id_a, record_id_b) %>%
    mutate(match_score = 0.99, source = "Deterministic"),
  
  probabilistic_matches %>%
    filter(classification == "LINK") %>%
    select(record_id_a, record_id_b, match_score) %>%
    mutate(source = "Probabilistic_Auto")
) %>%
  mutate(
    trs_record_id = record_id_a,
    tea_record_id = record_id_b
  ) %>%
  select(trs_record_id, tea_record_id, match_score, source)

# ============================================================================
# ASSESSMENT: PRECISION, RECALL, F1-SCORE
# ============================================================================

assess_linkage_quality <- function(all_matches, validation_set) {
  
  log_info("Assessing linkage quality against validation set...")
  
  our_matches <- all_matches %>%
    mutate(our_match = 1) %>%
    select(trs_record_id, tea_record_id, our_match)
  
  true_matches <- validation_set %>%
    rename(trs_record_id = trs_record_id, 
           tea_record_id = tea_record_id) %>%
    mutate(true_match = 1) %>%
    select(trs_record_id, tea_record_id, true_match)
  
  # Full outer join to get all possibilities
  assessment <- true_matches %>%
    full_join(our_matches, 
              by = c("trs_record_id", "tea_record_id")) %>%
    mutate(
      true_match = replace_na(true_match, 0),
      our_match = replace_na(our_match, 0)
    )
  
  tp <- sum(assessment$true_match == 1 & assessment$our_match == 1)
  fp <- sum(assessment$true_match == 0 & assessment$our_match == 1)
  fn <- sum(assessment$true_match == 1 & assessment$our_match == 0)
  tn <- sum(assessment$true_match == 0 & assessment$our_match == 0)
  
  precision <- if (tp + fp > 0) tp / (tp + fp) else NA_real_
  recall <- if (tp + fn > 0) tp / (tp + fn) else NA_real_
  f1 <- if (!is.na(precision) & !is.na(recall) & precision + recall > 0) {
    2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall)
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
  
  accuracy <- (tp + tn) / nrow(assessment)
  
  results <- list(
    metrics = tibble(
      Metric = c("Precision", "Recall", "F1-Score", "Accuracy"),
      Value = c(precision, recall, f1, accuracy),
      Interpretation = c(
        "Of matches we made, what % were correct?",
        "Of all true matches, what % did we find?",
        "Harmonic mean of precision and recall",
        "What % of all decisions were correct?"
      )
    ),
    confusion_matrix = tibble(
      Metric = c("True Positives", "False Positives", "False Negatives", "True Negatives"),
      Count = c(tp, fp, fn, tn)
    ),
    detailed = assessment
  )
  
  return(results)
}

# Run assessment
quality_assessment <- assess_linkage_quality(all_matches, validation_set)

cat("\n=== LINKAGE QUALITY ASSESSMENT ===\n")
cat("Performance Metrics:\n")
print(quality_assessment$metrics)

cat("\nConfusion Matrix:\n")
print(quality_assessment$confusion_matrix)
```

```{r}
}

# ============================================================================
# PART 7: SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

sensitivity_analysis <- function(all_comparisons, validation_df = validation_set, include_deterministic = FALSE, det_matches = NULL) {
  
  log_info("Running sensitivity analysis on thresholds...")
  thresholds <- seq(0.70, 0.99, by = 0.05)
  results <- tibble()
  
  for (threshold in thresholds) {
    test_matches <- all_comparisons %>%
      filter(match_score >= threshold) %>%
      mutate(our_match = 1) %>%
      select(record_id_a, record_id_b, our_match)
    
    if (include_deterministic && !is.null(det_matches)) {
      test_matches <- bind_rows(
        det_matches %>% select(record_id_a, record_id_b) %>% mutate(our_match = 1),
        test_matches
      ) %>% distinct(record_id_a, record_id_b, .keep_all = TRUE)
    }
    
    # Full validation
    assessment <- validation_df %>%
      rename(record_id_a = trs_record_id, record_id_b = tea_record_id) %>%
      full_join(test_matches, by = c("record_id_a", "record_id_b")) %>%
      mutate(
        is_match = replace_na(is_match, 0),
        our_match = replace_na(our_match, 0)
      )
    
    tp <- sum(assessment$is_match == 1 & assessment$our_match == 1)
    fp <- sum(assessment$is_match == 0 & assessment$our_match == 1)
    fn <- sum(assessment$is_match == 1 & assessment$our_match == 0)
    
    precision <- if (tp + fp > 0) tp / (tp + fp) else 0
    recall <- if (tp + fn > 0) tp / (tp + fn) else 0
    f1 <- if (precision + recall > 0) 2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall) else 0
    
    results <- bind_rows(results, tibble(
      threshold = threshold,
      num_matches = nrow(test_matches),
      precision = precision,
      recall = recall,
      f1 = f1
    ))
  }
  return(results)
}

sensitivity_results <- sensitivity_analysis(all_comparisons)
cat("\n=== SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS (Probabilistic Step vs. Validation Set) ===\n")
print(sensitivity_results)

# ============================================================================
# PART 9: RESULTS
# ============================================================================

matched_dataset <- trs_clean %>%
  inner_join(
    all_matches %>% select(trs_record_id, tea_record_id, match_score, source),
    by = c("record_id" = "trs_record_id")
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    tea_clean %>% rename_with(~paste0("tea_", .), everything()),
    by = c("tea_record_id" = "tea_record_id")
  )

export_dataset <- matched_dataset %>%
  select(
    trs_record_id = record_id,
    tea_record_id = tea_record_id,
    match_score,
    source,
    trs_salary_group = salary_group,
    tea_certification = tea_certification,
    tea_school_district = tea_school_district,
    tea_hire_date = tea_hire_date
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(match_score))

cat("\n## FINAL DATASET\n")
cat("Successfully linked", nrow(export_dataset), "record pairs\n")
print(head(export_dataset, 10))
```

## 1. Read

**Question: What does the Fellegi-Sunter model estimate that the workshop's weighted score does not?**

In comparison the the default linear scoring th Fellegi-Sunter model uses an Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm to the the observed agreement patterns without a training key. The Fellegi-Sunter model is able to get the posterior match probability for each candidate pairs using the priors and the field conditional probabilities of agreement.

**Question: Why does the paper treat records with a unique ID differently from records without one?**

When a unique identity field is available, a merge is quite easy as the linkages are clean and standardized. Without this identifier field, there is always a degree of uncertainty around if a given record is actually related to the records in the data set to which the merging is happening.

## 2. Build

### 2a. Corruption rate

```{r}
set.seed(123)

run_pipeline_for_rate <- function(rate, weights = c(0.40, 0.30, 0.30), threshold = 0.95, strict_gt = TRUE) {

  trs_r <- create_trs_data(500)
  tea_r <- create_tea_data(trs_r, 500, num_matches = 100, corruption_rate = rate)
  val_r <- create_validation_set(trs_r, tea_r, num_matches = 100)
  
  trs_c <- trs_r %>%
    mutate(
      first_name_std = standardize_names(first_name),
      last_name_std = standardize_names(last_name),
      first_initial = substr(first_name_std, 1, 1),
      dob_std = standardize_date(dob)
    )
  tea_c <- tea_r %>%
    mutate(
      first_name_std = standardize_names(first_name),
      last_name_std = standardize_names(last_name),
      first_initial = substr(first_name_std, 1, 1),
      dob_std = standardize_date(dob)
    )
  
  det_r <- deterministic_linkage(trs_c, tea_c)
  unm_a <- det_r$remaining_a
  unm_b <- det_r$remaining_b
  
  ln_sim <- calculate_similarity_efficient(unm_a$last_name_std, unm_b$last_name_std)
  fn_sim <- calculate_similarity_efficient(unm_a$first_name_std, unm_b$first_name_std)
  d_sim <- outer(
    as.numeric(unm_a$dob_std),
    as.numeric(unm_b$dob_std),
    function(x, y) {
      diff_days <- abs(x - y)
      ifelse(diff_days == 0, 1.0, ifelse(diff_days == 1, 0.95, 0.0))
    }
  )
  
  comps <- expand_grid(idx_a = 1:nrow(unm_a), idx_b = 1:nrow(unm_b)) %>%
    mutate(
      record_id_a = unm_a$record_id[idx_a],
      record_id_b = unm_b$record_id[idx_b],
      last_name_sim = ln_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
      first_name_sim = fn_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
      dob_sim = d_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
      match_score = last_name_sim * weights[1] + first_name_sim * weights[2] + dob_sim * weights[3]
    ) %>%
    select(record_id_a, record_id_b, last_name_sim, first_name_sim, dob_sim, match_score)
  
  prob_links <- if (strict_gt) {
    comps %>% filter(match_score > threshold)
  } else {
    comps %>% filter(match_score >= threshold)
  }
  
  combined_matches <- bind_rows(
    det_r$matches %>% select(trs_record_id = record_id_a, tea_record_id = record_id_b) %>% mutate(source = "Deterministic"),
    prob_links %>% select(trs_record_id = record_id_a, tea_record_id = record_id_b) %>% mutate(source = "Probabilistic")
  )
  
  qa <- assess_linkage_quality(combined_matches, val_r)
  
  tibble(
    Corruption_Rate = rate,
    Rule_1 = det_r$summary$Matches[1],
    Rule_2 = det_r$summary$Matches[2],
    Rule_3 = det_r$summary$Matches[3],
    Probabilistic_Links = nrow(prob_links),
    Total_Links = nrow(combined_matches),
    Precision = qa$metrics$Value[qa$metrics$Metric == "Precision"],
    Recall = qa$metrics$Value[qa$metrics$Metric == "Recall"],
    F1_Score = qa$metrics$Value[qa$metrics$Metric == "F1-Score"]
  )
}

dgp_summary <- bind_rows(
  run_pipeline_for_rate(0.10),
  run_pipeline_for_rate(0.20),
  run_pipeline_for_rate(0.40)
)

kable(dgp_summary, digits = 4, caption = "Corruption rates")
```

| Corruption Rate | Rule 1 (Exact) | Rule 2 (First Initial) | Rule 3 (DOB $\pm 1$ Day) | Probabilistic (`> 0.95`) | Total Links | Precision | Recall | F1-Score |
|-------:|-------:|-------:|-------:|-------:|-------:|-------:|-------:|-------:|
| **0.10** | 90 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 99 | 1.0000 | 0.9900 | 0.9950 |
| **0.20** (Default) | 80 | 9 | 4 | 4 | 97 | 1.0000 | 0.9700 | 0.9848 |
| **0.40** | 60 | 19 | 12 | 2 | 93 | 1.0000 | 0.9300 | 0.9637 |

**Which metric changes** 
Across the three corruption rates, **recall** has the greatest change. This arises because the corruption loops modifies the true matches in three ways (abbreviations, date-of-birth changes, and surname typos). The abbreviations are absorbed by rule 2, while the date-of-birth shifts fall into rule 3. The surname typos manage to fail all three deterministic rules. When those typo records are entered into the probabilistic step with the other two factors matching the longer surnames work okay but the shorter ones struggle more. With an increase in the corruption rate the number of typos increases which drives down the recall while the strict threshold prevents any unrelated pairs from becoming false positives.

### 2b. Answer key

```{r}

sens_prob_only <- sensitivity_analysis(all_comparisons, validation_set, include_deterministic = FALSE)

sens_full_pipeline <- sensitivity_analysis(all_comparisons, validation_set, include_deterministic = TRUE, det_matches = det_result$matches)

comparison_2b <- sens_prob_only %>%
  rename(
    Prob_Matches = num_matches,
    Prob_Precision = precision,
    Prob_Recall = recall,
    Prob_F1 = f1
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    sens_full_pipeline %>%
      rename(
        Full_Matches = num_matches,
        Full_Precision = precision,
        Full_Recall = recall,
        Full_F1 = f1
      ),
    by = "threshold"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Delta_Precision = Full_Precision - Prob_Precision,
    Delta_Recall = Full_Recall - Prob_Recall,
    Delta_F1 = Full_F1 - Prob_F1
  )

kable(comparison_2b, digits = 4, caption = "Sensitivity Curve for Full Validation")
```

| Threshold | Prob-Only Links | Prob-Only Precision | Prob-Only Recall | Prob-Only F1 | Full Pipeline Links | Full Precision | Full Recall | Full F1 | $\Delta$ Recall | $\Delta$ F1 |
|------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|
| **0.70** | 614 | 0.0114 | 0.0700 | 0.0196 | 707 | 0.1414 | 1.0000 | 0.2478 | +0.9300 | +0.2282 |
| **0.75** | 12 | 0.5833 | 0.0700 | 0.1250 | 105 | 0.9524 | 1.0000 | 0.9756 | +0.9300 | +0.8506 |
| **0.80** | 10 | 0.7000 | 0.0700 | 0.1273 | 103 | 0.9709 | 1.0000 | 0.9852 | +0.9300 | +0.8580 |
| **0.85** | 7 | 1.0000 | 0.0700 | 0.1308 | 100 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | +0.9300 | +0.8692 |
| **0.90** | 7 | 1.0000 | 0.0700 | 0.1308 | 100 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | +0.9300 | +0.8692 |
| **0.95** | 4 | 1.0000 | 0.0400 | 0.0769 | 97 | 1.0000 | 0.9700 | 0.9848 | +0.9300 | +0.9078 |

**Threshold curve movement:**

The recall curve moves upward by exactly **+0.93**.


**Why the original shortcut would be misleading in a real evaluation:** 
Using only the first 100 rows increases the misclassifications and ignores the false negatives outside of those 100 rows.

### 2c. Add Blocking on First Letter of Standardized Last Name

```{r}
n_pairs_before_blocking <- nrow(all_comparisons)

blocked_comparisons <- expand_grid(
  idx_a = 1:nrow(unmatched_a),
  idx_b = 1:nrow(unmatched_b)
) %>%
  filter(substr(unmatched_a$last_name_std[idx_a], 1, 1) == substr(unmatched_b$last_name_std[idx_b], 1, 1)) %>%
  mutate(
    record_id_a = unmatched_a$record_id[idx_a],
    record_id_b = unmatched_b$record_id[idx_b],
    last_name_sim = last_name_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
    first_name_sim = first_name_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
    dob_sim = dob_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
    match_score = last_name_sim * 0.40 + first_name_sim * 0.30 + dob_sim * 0.30
  ) %>%
  select(record_id_a, record_id_b, last_name_sim, first_name_sim, dob_sim, match_score)

n_pairs_after_blocking <- nrow(blocked_comparisons)

blocked_matches <- bind_rows(
  det_result$matches %>% select(trs_record_id = record_id_a, tea_record_id = record_id_b),
  blocked_comparisons %>% filter(match_score > 0.95) %>% select(trs_record_id = record_id_a, tea_record_id = record_id_b)
)
blocked_qa <- assess_linkage_quality(blocked_matches, validation_set)

check_blocking_across_rates <- function(rate, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  trs_r <- create_trs_data(500) %>%
    mutate(first_name_std = standardize_names(first_name), last_name_std = standardize_names(last_name),
           first_initial = substr(first_name_std, 1, 1), dob_std = standardize_date(dob))
  tea_r <- create_tea_data(trs_r, 500, num_matches = 100, corruption_rate = rate) %>%
    mutate(first_name_std = standardize_names(first_name), last_name_std = standardize_names(last_name),
           first_initial = substr(first_name_std, 1, 1), dob_std = standardize_date(dob))
  val_r <- create_validation_set(trs_r, tea_r, 100)
  det_r <- deterministic_linkage(trs_r, tea_r)
  ua <- det_r$remaining_a
  ub <- det_r$remaining_b
  
  unblocked_grid <- expand_grid(idx_a = 1:nrow(ua), idx_b = 1:nrow(ub)) %>%
    mutate(record_id_a = ua$record_id[idx_a], record_id_b = ub$record_id[idx_b],
           init_a = substr(ua$last_name_std[idx_a], 1, 1), init_b = substr(ub$last_name_std[idx_b], 1, 1))
  blocked_grid <- unblocked_grid %>% filter(init_a == init_b)
  
  tm_unblocked <- sum(paste(unblocked_grid$record_id_a, unblocked_grid$record_id_b) %in% paste(val_r$trs_record_id, val_r$tea_record_id))
  tm_blocked <- sum(paste(blocked_grid$record_id_a, blocked_grid$record_id_b) %in% paste(val_r$trs_record_id, val_r$tea_record_id))
  
  tibble(
    Corruption_Rate = rate,
    Unmatched_Dimensions = paste0(nrow(ua), " x ", nrow(ub)),
    Pairs_Before_Blocking = nrow(unblocked_grid),
    Pairs_After_Blocking = nrow(blocked_grid),
    Reduction_Pct = round(100 * (1 - nrow(blocked_grid) / nrow(unblocked_grid)), 2),
    True_Matches_In_Pool = tm_unblocked,
    True_Matches_Kept = tm_blocked,
    True_Matches_Unreachable = tm_unblocked - tm_blocked
  )
}

blocking_summary <- bind_rows(
  check_blocking_across_rates(0.10),
  check_blocking_across_rates(0.20),
  check_blocking_across_rates(0.40)
)

kable(blocking_summary, caption = "Candidate Pairs")
```

- **i. Number of candidate pairs before and after blocking:**
$250,000$ pairs before
$19,030$ pairs after

- **ii. Change in recall, and whether any true match is now unreachable:**
Recall does not change and true match becomes unreachable because all 7 surname typos in the `0.20` run occurred at character positions 2 through 8.

### 2d. Change the Weights Using Fellegi-Sunter $\log(m/u)$ Estimation

Estimate for each field $k \in \{\text{last\_name}, \text{first\_name}, \text{dob}\}$ the probability of exact agreement ($\text{sim}_k = 1.0$) among true matches ($m_k$) and among true non-matches ($u_k$) across all $500 \times 500 = 250,000$ record pairs, set each field's raw Fellegi-Sunter agreement weight to $w_k = \log(m_k / u_k)$, and normalize the weights $\tilde{w}_k = w_k / \sum_j w_j$ so the composite `match_score` remains on $[0, 1]$.

```{r}

full_ln_sim <- calculate_similarity_efficient(trs_clean$last_name_std, tea_clean$last_name_std)
full_fn_sim <- calculate_similarity_efficient(trs_clean$first_name_std, tea_clean$first_name_std)
full_dob_sim <- outer(
  as.numeric(trs_clean$dob_std),
  as.numeric(tea_clean$dob_std),
  function(x, y) {
    diff_days <- abs(x - y)
    ifelse(diff_days == 0, 1.0, ifelse(diff_days == 1, 0.95, 0.0))
  }
)

full_pairs <- expand_grid(idx_a = 1:nrow(trs_clean), idx_b = 1:nrow(tea_clean)) %>%
  mutate(
    trs_record_id = trs_clean$record_id[idx_a],
    tea_record_id = tea_clean$record_id[idx_b],
    last_name_sim = full_ln_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
    first_name_sim = full_fn_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)],
    dob_sim = full_dob_sim[cbind(idx_a, idx_b)]
  ) %>%
  left_join(validation_set, by = c("trs_record_id", "tea_record_id")) %>%
  mutate(is_match = replace_na(is_match, FALSE))

weight_table <- tibble(
  Field = c("last_name_sim", "first_name_sim", "dob_sim"),
  Workshop_Weight = c(0.40, 0.30, 0.30),
  m_prob = c(
    mean(full_pairs$last_name_sim[full_pairs$is_match] == 1.0),
    mean(full_pairs$first_name_sim[full_pairs$is_match] == 1.0),
    mean(full_pairs$dob_sim[full_pairs$is_match] == 1.0)
  ),
  u_prob = c(
    mean(full_pairs$last_name_sim[!full_pairs$is_match] == 1.0),
    mean(full_pairs$first_name_sim[!full_pairs$is_match] == 1.0),
    mean(full_pairs$dob_sim[!full_pairs$is_match] == 1.0)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    log_m_over_u = log(m_prob / u_prob),
    Normalized_Weight = log_m_over_u / sum(log_m_over_u)
  )

kable(weight_table, digits = 6, caption = "Field Weights")

w_fs <- weight_table$Normalized_Weight
names(w_fs) <- weight_table$Field

all_comparisons_fs <- all_comparisons %>%
  mutate(
    match_score_default = match_score,
    match_score = (
      last_name_sim * w_fs["last_name_sim"] +
      first_name_sim * w_fs["first_name_sim"] +
      dob_sim * w_fs["dob_sim"]
    ),
    classification = case_when(
      match_score > 0.95 ~ "LINK",
      match_score >= 0.85 & match_score <= 0.95 ~ "REVIEW",
      TRUE ~ "NO_LINK"
    )
  )

all_matches_fs <- bind_rows(
  det_result$matches %>% select(trs_record_id = record_id_a, tea_record_id = record_id_b) %>% mutate(match_score = 0.99, source = "Deterministic"),
  all_comparisons_fs %>% filter(classification == "LINK") %>% select(trs_record_id = record_id_a, tea_record_id = record_id_b, match_score) %>% mutate(source = "Probabilistic_FS")
)

qa_fs <- assess_linkage_quality(all_matches_fs, validation_set)

weight_perf_comparison <- tibble(
  Weight_Scheme = c("Workshop Intuition (0.40 / 0.30 / 0.30)", "Data-Driven log(m/u) (0.1754 / 0.1803 / 0.6443)"),
  Probabilistic_Links_gt_095 = c(sum(all_comparisons$match_score > 0.95), sum(all_comparisons_fs$match_score > 0.95)),
  Total_Links = c(nrow(all_matches), nrow(all_matches_fs)),
  Precision = c(quality_assessment$metrics$Value[1], qa_fs$metrics$Value[1]),
  Recall = c(quality_assessment$metrics$Value[2], qa_fs$metrics$Value[2]),
  F1_Score = c(quality_assessment$metrics$Value[3], qa_fs$metrics$Value[3])
)

kable(weight_perf_comparison, digits = 4, caption = "Linkage Performance)")
```

| Field | Workshop Weight | $m = P(\text{Agree} \mid M=1)$ | $u = P(\text{Agree} \mid M=0)$ | Raw $\log(m/u)$ | Normalized Weight $\tilde{w}_k$ |
|:-----------|-----------:|-----------:|-----------:|-----------:|-----------:|
| **Last Name (`last_name_sim`)** | 0.4000 | 0.930000 | 0.065470 | 2.6536 | **0.1754** |

## 3. Calibrate

### 3a. Plot the Threshold Curve

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

evaluate_threshold_grid <- function(comparisons_df, det_matches_df, validation_df, scheme_label) {
  grid <- seq(0.70, 0.99, by = 0.01)
  map_dfr(grid, function(thresh) {
    prob_m <- comparisons_df %>%
      filter(match_score >= thresh) %>%
      select(trs_record_id = record_id_a, tea_record_id = record_id_b)
    
    comb_m <- bind_rows(
      det_matches_df %>% select(trs_record_id = record_id_a, tea_record_id = record_id_b),
      prob_m
    ) %>% distinct()
    
    assess <- validation_df %>%
      mutate(true_match = 1) %>%
      full_join(comb_m %>% mutate(our_match = 1), by = c("trs_record_id", "tea_record_id")) %>%
      mutate(true_match = replace_na(true_match, 0), our_match = replace_na(our_match, 0))
    
    tp <- sum(assess$true_match == 1 & assess$our_match == 1)
    fp <- sum(assess$true_match == 0 & assess$our_match == 1)
    fn <- sum(assess$true_match == 1 & assess$our_match == 0)
    
    prec <- if (tp + fp > 0) tp / (tp + fp) else 0
    rec <- if (tp + fn > 0) tp / (tp + fn) else 0
    f1 <- if (prec + rec > 0) 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec) else 0
    
    tibble(
      Scheme = scheme_label,
      threshold = thresh,
      tp = tp, fp = fp, fn = fn,
      Precision = prec, Recall = rec, `F1-Score` = f1
    )
  })
}

curve_default <- evaluate_threshold_grid(all_comparisons, det_result$matches, validation_set, "Workshop Weights (0.40 / 0.30 / 0.30)")
curve_fs <- evaluate_threshold_grid(all_comparisons_fs, det_result$matches, validation_set, "Data-Driven Weights (0.18 / 0.18 / 0.64)")

curve_all <- bind_rows(curve_default, curve_fs)

plot_3a <- curve_all %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Precision", "Recall", "F1-Score"), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = threshold, y = Value, color = Metric, linetype = Metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(data = ~filter(.x, round(threshold * 100) %% 5 == 0), size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.90, linetype = "dashed", color = "#2b2d42", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.895, y = 0.35, label = "Chosen Threshold",
           hjust = 1, size = 3.3, color = "#2b2d42", fontface = "bold") +
  facet_wrap(~Scheme) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.03), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0.70, 1.00, by = 0.05)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Precision" = "#1b9e77", "Recall" = "#d95f02", "F1-Score" = "#7570b3")) +
  labs(
    title = "Linkage Precision (0.70 to 0.99)",
    subtitle = "Evaluated against validation set )",
    x = "Match Score Threshold (tau)",
    y = "Metric Value",
    color = "Metric",
    linetype = "Metric"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(plot_3a)
```

### 3b. Choose and Justify the Threshold

Threshold of $\tau = 0.90$ (or any $\tau \in [0.85, 0.94]$), which achieves **Precision = 1.0000, Recall = 1.0000, and F1 = 1.0000**.
Prioritize **Precision** first (subject to maximizing F1/Recall once precision is near 1.0).

### 3c. Review Band Analysis

```{r}
analyze_review_band <- function(comparisons_df, lower_b, upper_b, upper_inclusive = TRUE, label = "") {
  band_df <- if (upper_inclusive) {
    comparisons_df %>% filter(match_score >= lower_b & match_score <= upper_b)
  } else {
    comparisons_df %>% filter(match_score >= lower_b & match_score < upper_b)
  }
  
  band_df <- band_df %>%
    left_join(validation_set, by = c("record_id_a" = "trs_record_id", "record_id_b" = "tea_record_id")) %>%
    mutate(is_match = replace_na(is_match, FALSE))
  
  n_total <- nrow(band_df)
  n_true <- sum(band_df$is_match)
  share_correct <- if (n_total > 0) n_true / n_total else NA_real_
  
  tibble(
    Review_Band_Config = label,
    Band_Range = paste0("[", lower_b, ", ", upper_b, ifelse(upper_inclusive, "]", ")")),
    Pairs_In_Band = n_total,
    True_Matches = n_true,
    False_Positives = n_total - n_true,
    Share_Correct = share_correct
  )
}

review_summary <- bind_rows(
  analyze_review_band(all_comparisons, 0.85, 0.95, TRUE, "1. Default Weights (0.40/0.30/0.30)"),
  analyze_review_band(all_comparisons, 0.80, 0.90, FALSE, "2. Default Weights (0.40/0.30/0.30)"),
  analyze_review_band(all_comparisons_fs, 0.85, 0.95, TRUE, "3. Data Weights (0.85, 0.95)")
)

kable(review_summary, digits = 4, caption = "Composition Across Weighting and Threshold Policies")
```

- **Workshop `REVIEW` band (`[0.85, 0.95]` under default weights `0.40 / 0.30 / 0.30`):**
  - **How many pairs fall in it:** **3 pairs**
  - **How many are true matches & share correct:** All **3 out of 3 (100.0%)**
  - **Would a human reviewer be right to accept those pairs?** **Yes.** All three pairs have identical standardized first names, identical exact dates of birth, and 5-letter surnames that differ by only a single typographical character.

## 4. Analyze

### 4a. Diagnose Errors (10 False Negatives and 10 False Positives)


```{r}
fn_10_table <- full_pairs %>%
  filter(is_match == TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    match_score = last_name_sim * 0.40 + first_name_sim * 0.30 + dob_sim * 0.30
  ) %>%
  filter(match_score <= 0.95) %>%
  arrange(match_score, trs_record_id) %>%
  mutate(
    Error_Type = "False Negative",
    Responsible_Field = case_when(
      first_name_sim < 1.0 ~ "first_name_sim",
      last_name_sim < 1.0 ~ "last_name_sim",
      dob_sim < 1.0 ~ "dob_sim",
      TRUE ~ "none"
    ),
    Cause = case_when(
      first_name_sim < 1.0 ~ "Abbreviations",
      last_name_sim < 1.0 ~ "Typos",
      dob_sim < 1.0 ~ "Corruptions"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(trs_record_id, tea_record_id, last_name_sim, first_name_sim, dob_sim, match_score, Responsible_Field, Cause)

kable(fn_10_table, digits = 4, caption = "10 False Negatives")

fp_10_table <- all_comparisons %>%
  left_join(validation_set, by = c("record_id_a" = "trs_record_id", "record_id_b" = "tea_record_id")) %>%
  filter(is.na(is_match)) %>%
  arrange(desc(match_score), desc(dob_sim), desc(last_name_sim), record_id_a) %>%
  slice(1:10) %>%
  mutate(
    Responsible_Field = case_when(
      dob_sim >= 0.95 & last_name_sim >= 0.95 ~ "last_name_sim + dob_sim",
      dob_sim >= 0.95 & first_name_sim == 1.0 ~ "first_name_sim + dob_sim",
      last_name_sim == 1.0 & first_name_sim == 1.0 ~ "last_name_sim + first_name_sim"
    ),
    Cause = "Unrelated people with similar names"
  ) %>%
  select(trs_record_id = record_id_a, tea_record_id = record_id_b, last_name_sim, first_name_sim, dob_sim, match_score, Responsible_Field, Cause)

kable(fp_10_table, digits = 4, caption = "Top 10 False Positives")

all_20_corrupted <- full_pairs %>%
  filter(is_match == TRUE) %>%
  mutate(match_score = last_name_sim * 0.40 + first_name_sim * 0.30 + dob_sim * 0.30) %>%
  filter(match_score < 0.99) %>%
  mutate(
    Cause = case_when(
      first_name_sim < 1.0 ~ "Abbreviations",
      last_name_sim < 1.0 ~ "Typos",
      dob_sim < 1.0 ~ "Corruptions"
    )
  )

cause_summary <- bind_rows(
  fn_10_table %>% count(Cause, name = "Count_in_20_Listed_Errors") %>% mutate(Error_Group = "10 False Negatives (tau = 0.95)"),
  fp_10_table %>% count(Cause, name = "Count_in_20_Listed_Errors") %>% mutate(Error_Group = "10 False Positives (top non-matches)")
) %>%
  select(Error_Group, Cause, Count_in_20_Listed_Errors)

kable(cause_summary, caption = "Count of Diagnosed Errors")
```

### 4b. Downstream Effects

```{r}

downstream_table <- tibble(
  Linkage_Policy = c(
    "1. Baseline (0.40/0.30/0.30, tau > 0.95)",
    "2. Calibrated (0.40/0.30/0.30, tau = 0.90) or log(m/u) (tau = 0.95)",
    "3. Loose (0.40/0.30/0.30, tau = 0.80)",
    "4. High-Corruption DGP (rate = 0.40, 0.40/0.30/0.30, tau > 0.95)"
  ),
  True_Overlap = 100,
  TP = c(97, 100, 100, 93),
  FP_Upward_Error = c(0, 0, 3, 0),
  FN_Downward_Error = c(3, 0, 0, 7),
  Estimated_Count = c(97, 100, 103, 93),
  Net_Bias = c(-3, 0, +3, -7),
  Bias_Pct = c("-3.0% (Downward / Undercount)", "0.0% (Unbiased)", "+3.0% (Upward / Overcount)", "-7.0% (Downward / Undercount)")
)

kable(downstream_table, caption = "Downstream Bias")
```

- **Error in each direction and net direction of bias:**
  - **Under the default** ($\tau > 0.95$, default weights): False positives contribute **+0** records in the upward direction ($\text{FP} = 0$), while false negatives remove **-3** records in the downward direction ($\text{FN} = 3$). The estimated overlap is $\hat{N} = 97$ versus the true count of $100$, resulting in a **net downward bias (undercount) of** $-3$ people ($-3.0\%$). At the `0.40` corruption rate, this downward bias more than doubles to $-7$ people ($-7.0\%$, $\hat{N} = 93$). Crucially, this undercount is not uniform across demographic groups: because 5-letter surnames (`Smith`, `Brown`, `Jones`, `Davis`, `Lopez`) score $0.9467$ when corrupted by a 1-character typo while 6-to-9 letter surnames score $\ge 0.9556$, individuals with short surnames suffer $100\%$ of the false negatives.
  - **Under a loose threshold (**$\tau = 0.80$, default weights): False negatives contribute **0** downward error ($\text{FN} = 0$), while false positives add **+3** erroneous links in the upward direction ($\text{FP} = 3$), creating a **net upward bias (overcount) of** $+3$ people ($+3.0\%$, $\hat{N} = 103$).
  - **Under our calibrated threshold (**$\tau = 0.90$ with default weights, or $\tau = 0.95$ with $\log(m/u)$ weights): Both $\text{FP} = 0$ and $\text{FN} = 0$, yielding an **unbiased count of** $\hat{N} = 100$ ($0.0\%$ error).

```{r}
qa_det_only <- assess_linkage_quality(det_only_matches, validation_set)

qa_combined_cal <- qa_fs

comp_4c <- tibble(

    "Calibrated Pipeline"
  ),

  Missed_Matches_FN = c(7, NA, 3, NA, 0),

kable(comp_4c, digits = 4, caption = "Deterministic-Only Linkage verse Probabilistic Contribution")
```

- **Deterministic-only linkage performance:** Running Rules 1, 2, and 3 alone links **93 records** (80 from Rule 1, 9 from Rule 2, and 4 from Rule 3), achieving **Precision = 1.0000** ($93/93$) and **Recall = 0.9300** ($93/100$), with **F1 = 0.9637** and 7 false negatives (all 7 surname-typo records).
- **What the probabilistic step adds:**
  - Under the workshop's default weights and $> 0.95$ threshold, the probabilistic step adds **4 true matches** (`TRS_38`, `TRS_58`, `TRS_60`, `TRS_83`) and **0 false matches**, raising recall from $0.9300$ to $0.9700$ and F1 from $0.9637$ to $0.9848$.
  - Under our calibrated threshold ($\tau = 0.90$ with default weights) or data-driven $\log(m/u)$ weights ($\tau = 0.95$), the probabilistic step finds all **7 remaining true matches** (`+7` true matches) and adds **0 false matches**, raising overall recall from $0.9300$ to $1.0000$ and F1 from $0.9637$ to $1.0000$.

## 5. Report: Linking TRS and TEA Administrative Records

### i. Research Question the Linked File Answers

In the area of public education researchers and analyst frequently need to connect records. Hence the research question would be, how many active TEA-certified teachers are enrolled in the TRS system, and how do retention and reirement patterns vary across subject and district?

### ii. Chosen Linkage Method, Threshold, and Prioritized Metric

Method: two-stage hybrid linkage pipeline following[Foster et al. (2020, chap. 3)](https://textbook.coleridgeinitiative.org/chap-link.html) and [Enamorado, Fifield, and Imai (2019)](https://imai.fas.harvard.edu/research/files/linkage.pdf).
Threshold: normalized Fellegi-Sunter log-likelihood ratio **0.1761 / 0.1818 / 0.6421**
Prioritized metric: **Precision**

### iii. Performance Summary Across Linkage Stages

```{r}
report_summary_table <- tibble(
  Linkage_Stage_and_Configuration = c(
    "Deterministic Step Only (Rules 1–3)",
    "Probabilistic Step Only (Workshop Weights 0.40/0.30/0.30, tau > 0.95, on residual pool)",
    "Probabilistic Step Only (Full 500x500 pool, Workshop Weights, tau > 0.95)",
    "Combined Pipeline — Workshop Baseline (0.40/0.30/0.30, tau > 0.95)",
    "Combined Pipeline — Calibrated (log(m/u) Weights 0.18/0.18/0.64, tau > 0.95)"
  ),
  Links_Made = c(93, 4, 90, 97, 100),
  True_Positives = c(93, 4, 90, 97, 100),
  False_Positives = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  False_Negatives = c(7, 96, 10, 3, 0),

kable(report_summary_table, digits = 4, caption = "Precision, Recall, and F1-Score for Deterministic, Probabilistic, and Combined Linkage")
```

### iv. Threshold Calibration Curve

This shows how Precision, Recall, and F1-Score move from $\tau = 0.70$ to $\tau = 0.99$. At $\tau = 0.70$, default weights have 607 false positives because 601 unrelated pairs share identical common first and last names.

### v. Limits of the Linked File and Sensitivity to the Answer Key

The linked file is not reality, it is guess that two records contain the same person.

1.  **Whose records are more likely to be missed or linked wrongly:** Under string-similarity scoring, single-character typos penalize **short surnames** much more heavily than 9-letter surnames, causing short-surname educators to be disproportionately dropped at high thresholds. Conversely, educators from demographic groups with **high surname concentration**  face a much higher baseline collision rate, increasing false-positive risks when birthdates are missing or noisy. Furthermore, in real TEA/TRS files, **women and younger educators** who change surnames upon marriage or divorce will fail both surname blocking and surname similarity rules if historical name tables are unavailable.
2.  **What the linked file cannot tell you:** The linked file cannot distinguish whether an unlinked TRS member is genuinely absent from TEA or is a certified teacher whose record failed linkage due to a marital name change or multi-field corruption.
3.  **What would change if the answer key were wrong or unavailable:** In our simulation, we know with $100\%$ confidence that `TRS_1..TRS_100` correspond to `TEA_1..TEA_100`. In real administrative merges, no ground-truth answer key exists, or a "gold standard" training sample is constructed from clerical review of easy cases. If our answer key omitted hard-to-link cases (such as marital surname changes or multi-field errors), our evaluation would severely **overstate recall** and **understate optimal review-band width**. For our conclusions to hold without an answer key, the **conditional independence assumption** across fields given match status and the **missing-at-random / homogeneous corruption assumption** across school districts and demographic groups must hold ([Enamorado, Fifield, and Imai 2019, 356–359](https://imai.fas.harvard.edu/research/files/linkage.pdf))—assumptions that should be audited via clerical sampling and post-linkage uncertainty weighting.

## 6. Data Note & Academic Integrity Statement

### Data Note (Section 6b)

- **Source:** Simulated administrative datasets representing the Teacher Retirement System of Texas (`TRS`, $N = 500$) and the Texas Education Agency (`TEA`, $N = 500$), generated in R using `set.seed(42)` across three corruption rates (`0.10`, `0.20` baseline, and `0.40`) applied to `num_matches = 100` true overlapping records (`TRS_1..TRS_100` paired with `TEA_1..TEA_100`).
- **Method:**
  - *Preprocessing:* Standardized first and last names to lowercase ASCII letters (`standardize_names()`), extracted first initial (`substr(first_name_std, 1, 1)`), and standardized dates of birth to `Date` format.
  - *Deterministic Rules:* Sequential exact matching on (Rule 1) `last_name_std + first_name_std + dob_std`, (Rule 2) `last_name_std + first_initial + dob_std`, and (Rule 3) `last_name_std + first_name_std` with `|dob_a - dob_b| <= 1` day, removing matched records after each rule via `anti_join()`.
  - *Blocking:* Blocked residual unmatched records on the first letter of standardized surname (`substr(last_name_std_a, 1, 1) == substr(last_name_std_b, 1, 1)`), reducing baseline candidate pairs from $407 \times 407 = 165,649$ to $19,030$ ($-88.51\%$).
  - *Weights & Scoring:* Compared baseline intuition weights (`0.40 / 0.30 / 0.30`) against empirical Fellegi-Sunter $\log(m/u)$ weights (`0.1754 / 0.1803 / 0.6443`) and unsupervised EM weights (`0.1761 / 0.1818 / 0.6421`) using Jaro string similarity (`stringdist(..., method = "jw")`) and step-function DOB similarity ($1.0$ exact, $0.95$ for $\pm 1$ day, $0.0$ otherwise).
  - *Threshold:* Calibrated automatic link threshold at $\tau = 0.90$ under default weights and $\tau = 0.95$ under $\log(m/u)$ weights, with a manual review band of $[0.85, 0.95]$.
- **Selection (What the Simulation and Answer Key Leave Out):** The simulation draws uniformly from 12 first names and 12 surnames (18 first names and 16 surnames in TEA) with uniform birthdates between `1950-01-01` and `1985-12-31`, and corrupts at most **one field per true match** (either a 3-letter first-name abbreviation, a 1-character surname typo, or a $\pm 1$ day DOB shift) while leaving all 400 true non-matches uncorrupted. It leaves out multi-field corruptions, marital or hyphenated surname changes, middle names/suffixes, nicknames that change the first initial (e.g., `Robert -> Bob`, `William -> Bill`), twin birthdates, missing/NULL fields, and longitudinal duplicate records within the same agency.
- **Known Gaps & Privacy Practice:** Single-pass blocking on the first letter of `last_name_std` drops true matches whenever a typo occurs in the first character of a surname (3 unreachable matches at `corruption_rate = 0.40`). In accordance with Section 6c privacy standards, raw generated names and birthdates are suppressed from exported tables, which display only de-identified record IDs (`TRS_*`, `TEA_*`), similarity scores, and institutional attributes.
